verses.text: That same day Jesus went out of the house and sat down by the lake.
Such large crowds gathered around him that he got into a boat and sat in it. All the people stood on the shore.
Then he told them many things using stories. He said, "A farmer went out to plant his seed.
As he was scattering the seed, some fell along the path, and birds came and ate it up.
Some fell on rocky ground, where there was not much soil. It grew up quickly, because the soil was not deep.
But when the sun came up, the plants were scorched. They dried up because they had no roots.
Other seed fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked the plants.
But other seed fell on good soil, and it produced a crop. Some produced a hundred times as much as was planted, some sixty times and some thirty times.
Whoever has ears should listen."
The followers came to him and asked, "Why do you use stories when you speak to the people?"
He answered, "You have been given the gift of knowing the secrets of the kingdom of heaven, but they have not.
Whoever has something will be given more, and they will have plenty. But whoever does not have anything, even what they have will be taken away from them.
This is why I use stories when I speak to them: 'They look, but they do not really see. They listen, but they do not really hear or understand.'
In them the words of the prophet Isaiah come true: 'You will keep on hearing, but you will never understand. You will keep on looking, but you will never really see.

The hearts of these people have become hard. Their ears can hardly hear, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears and understand with their hearts. Then they would turn back to me, and I would heal them.'
But your eyes are blessed because they see, and your ears are blessed because they hear.
I tell you for certain, many prophets and good people wanted to see what you see, but they did not see it. They wanted to hear what you hear, but they did not hear it.
"So listen to what the story of the farmer means.
When anyone hears the message about the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was planted in their heart. This is the seed that fell along the path.
The seed that fell on rocky ground is the person who hears the message and accepts it with joy straight away.
But they have no roots, so they last only a short time. When trouble or hard times come because of the message, they quickly give up.
The seed that fell among the thorns is the person who hears the message, but the worries of this life and the lie that money brings happiness choke the message. So it produces nothing.
But the seed that fell on good soil is the person who hears the message and understands it. They produce a crop of a hundred, sixty or thirty times as much as was planted."
Jesus told them another story. "The kingdom of heaven is like a man who planted good seed in his field.
But while everyone was sleeping, his enemy came and planted weeds among the wheat, and then went away.
When the wheat came up and formed heads of grain, the weeds also appeared.
"The owner's servants came to him and said, 'Sir, did you not plant good seed in your field? So where did the weeds come from?'
"'An enemy did this,' he replied. "The servants asked him, 'Do you want us to go and pull the weeds up?'
"'No,' he answered. 'While you are pulling up the weeds, you might pull up the wheat with them.
Let both grow together until the harvest. At that time I will tell the workers, "First gather the weeds and tie them in bundles to be burned. Then gather the wheat and bring it into my barn."'"
Jesus told them another story. "The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man planted in his field.
It is the smallest of all seeds. But when it grows, it is the biggest of all garden plants. It becomes a tree, and the birds come and make nests in its branches."
He told them another story. "The kingdom of heaven is like yeast that a woman mixed into a large amount of flour, until the yeast worked its way all through the dough."
Jesus used stories to tell the crowd all these things. He did not say anything to them without using a story.
This made come true what the prophet had said: "I will speak using stories. I will tell things that have been hidden since the world was made."
Then Jesus left the crowd and went into the house. His followers came to him and said, "Explain to us the story of the weeds in the field."
He answered, "The one who planted the good seed is the Son of Man.
The field is the world. The good seed stands for the people who belong to the kingdom. The weeds are the people who belong to the evil one.
The enemy who plants the weeds is the devil. The harvest is the end of the world, and the workers are angels.
"The weeds are pulled up and burned in the fire. That is how it will be at the end of the world.
The Son of Man will send out his angels. They will remove from his kingdom everything that causes sin, and all who do evil.
They will throw them into the blazing furnace. There people will cry and grind their teeth.
Then the people who do what is right will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom. Whoever has ears should listen.
"The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. When a man found it, he hid it again. Then, full of joy, he went and sold everything he had and bought that field.
"Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a trader who was looking for fine pearls.
When he found one pearl that was worth a great deal, he went away and sold everything he had and bought it.
"Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that was thrown into the lake and caught all kinds of fish.
When it was full, the fishermen pulled it up on the shore. Then they sat down and put the good fish in baskets, but threw the bad ones away.
That is how it will be at the end of the world. The angels will come and separate the evil people from the people who do what is right.
They will throw the evil ones into the blazing furnace. There people will cry and grind their teeth."
Jesus asked, "Have you understood all these things?" "Yes, Lord," they replied.
He said to them, "So every teacher of the law who has become a follower in the kingdom of heaven is like the owner of a house. He brings new treasures and old treasures out of his storeroom."
When Jesus had finished telling these stories, he left that place.
He went to his home town and began teaching the people in their synagogue. They were amazed and asked, "Where did this man get this wisdom and these miraculous powers?
Is he not the carpenter's son? Is his mother's name not Mary? Are his brothers not James, Joses, Simon and Judas?
Are all his sisters not here with us? So where did this man get all these things?"
And they refused to accept him. But Jesus said to them, "A prophet is honoured everywhere except in his own town and in his own home."
And he did not do many miracles there, because they did not believe in him.
